answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom. Shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five on top of those. Shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one on top. The resulting deck has 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, and 4 Conflict III cards; return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Result: a 10-card Conflict Deck — 1 Conflict I on top, 5 Conflict II below it, 4 Conflict III on the bottom. Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.’

answers.answer: In a four-player game, a human starts at 1 VP; in a three-player game, at 0 VP. In both, two Agents start on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops start in the garrison and nine in supply; the player takes 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track is ‘on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space’; place two Agents on the Leader and the third beside the board; three troops in garrison and ‘remaining nine’ in supply; ‘Take 1 water.’

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while you still have Agents. After taking a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the Reveal boxes of the cards revealed from your remaining hand; Agent-turn cards use their Agent boxes. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both kinds of turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents’ and after Reveal ‘your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.’ Reveal Turn: effects are from ‘just-revealed cards only’; Clean Up moves all cards from Agent and Reveal turns to the discard pile.

answers.answer: No. Any destination cost must be paid immediately before resolving any effects of the space or the played card, so an Agent-box effect cannot first generate resources to pay the entry cost. One card can send only one Agent, using one chosen Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: costs must be paid ‘before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played’; ‘You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents’; a card with no Agent icons ‘may only be revealed on a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: At a Combat space, all three troops recruited this turn may deploy, plus up to two troops from the garrison: five total in this example. At a non-Combat space, recruited troops remain in the garrison because deployment is allowed when sending an Agent to a Combat space. Recruited troops come from supply and are placed in the garrison first.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruit a troop ‘from your supply and place it in your garrison’; at a Combat space deploy ‘any or all units recruited during your current turn … plus up to two more units from your garrison.’

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; the Spy stays there. Infiltrate is an optional recall of your Spy from a connected post to ignore another player's Agent and send your Agent to that occupied space. Gather Intelligence is an optional recall of a connected Spy whenever you send an Agent, to draw a card; choose it immediately after placing the Agent and before resolving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both effects, but two different Spies may be recalled for the different effects on one placement. Gather Intelligence cannot be chosen after receiving the placement's effects.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spy Agent icon permits a connected space ‘you do not recall the Spy’; Infiltrate ignores the other player's Agent; Gather Intelligence is decided ‘immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects)’; the same Spy cannot be recalled for both, though one Spy may be used for each different effect.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm 3, and four revealed swords 4. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0 even if revealed swords remain. With no unit in the Conflict, you cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window, which is for players with at least one unit there.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop is 2, sandworm 3, and revealed sword 1; ‘You must have at least one unit in the Conflict to have any strength; if your last unit is ever removed, your strength becomes 0.’ Combat Intrigue is for each player with ‘at least one unit in the Conflict.’

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you from acting again later in the phase. The window closes when all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, after which Combat resolves. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not their garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: ‘You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier in the phase’; resolve after all involved pass consecutively. Combat cleanup returns troops to supply and sandworms to the bank.

answers.answer: In a four-player Conflict, two players tied for first each take the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card, and the remaining players compete for the third reward. In a three-player Conflict, the tied players each take the second reward and no other rewards are given; nobody takes the Conflict card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players each gain the second reward and ‘no one wins the Conflict or takes the Conflict card’; in games with three or fewer players ‘no other rewards are given’; in four players, exactly two tied for first leave the remaining players competing for third. Resolve Combat: ‘A player with 0 strength receives no reward.’

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards you take; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on Conflict cards are not doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time to receive it again: spend 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP. The summary does not say that the optional second payment is required.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: ‘if you have one or more sandworms … double the rewards’; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. Its example permits paying 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2.

answers.answer: Check for a match after you win the Conflict and take its card into your supply. A normal match is with a face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply bearing the same battle icon; if present, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During the Endgame, you may match the wild battle icon with any one of the three battle icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP. The summary does not specify a timing for checking a wild match beyond ‘during the Endgame.’
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: ‘When you win a Conflict and take that card into your supply, check’ for a same-icon face-up Conflict or Objective; if present, you ‘must’ flip the pair. During Endgame, ‘you may match the wild battle icon’ with any one of the three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it if you fall below 2 and regain it upon reaching 2 again. At 4, the printed track bonus is retained if you fall below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. Separately, the first player to 4 receives the Alliance token and 1 VP; that VP follows the token. Merely tying the Alliance holder at 4 does not steal it. The FAQ also says that if the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied player takes the token; falling to 3 or lower loses it, transferring it to an eligible 4+ player or returning it to the board if none exists.
answers.evidence: Victory Points: at 2, ‘gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it when reaching 2 again’; at 4 the track bonus is retained below 4 and earned again on return, while Alliance VP follows the token. ‘Tying the holder does not steal it.’ FAQ describes holder Influence loss and falling to 3 or lower.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card, or split Persuasion from a single source across different cards. You may buy an Imperium Row replacement immediately if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile and is not used immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal Effects: Persuasion can be used ‘before, between, or after’ effects. Acquiring Cards: Persuasion may be pooled or split; the Row refills so ‘you may acquire its replacement’; acquired cards go face up into the discard pile.

answers.answer: At the Makers phase, add 1 spice to each Maker space without an Agent; when you send an Agent to a Maker space, gain all bonus spice there. The Shield Wall prevents summoning a sandworm to a Conflict at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while it remains on the board; a detonation effect removes it. Maker Hooks are normally required where the sandworm icon specifies them, but they are not a universal prerequisite and are retained rather than spent. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, the space's listed choice is 1 or 2 sandworms respectively if you have Hooks; its base-spice option applies if not summoning. A sandworm is immediately deployed to your quadrant of the Conflict and can never be placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: unoccupied Maker spaces get 1 bonus spice, and an Agent gains all bonus spice. Sandworms: the Shield Wall restrictions apply; Hooks are not universal and ‘never spent’; a summoned worm is put in the Conflict and ‘can never be placed in a garrison.’ Board Space Guide lists Hagga's one- or Deep Desert's two-worm choice.

answers.answer: The Endgame is triggered at the end of a round if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Players first may play and resolve their Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare Victory Points. Tiebreakers are, in order: spice, Solari, water, and garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘At the end of a round’ with 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck, Endgame is triggered; first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then highest VP wins; tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has 2 contracts face up and 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 Intrigue cards to the Intrigue Deck and 4 Imperium cards to the Imperium Deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and are left out of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: flip two of 20 contracts face up and place the remaining 18 face down; shuffle 4 additional Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards into their decks; Shaddam is ‘an option’; contrasting-back contracts are a separate Rise of Ix set, left in the box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts into your supply and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. A Harvest contract requires sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining its specified total amount of spice that turn, including spice from other sources. An Immediate contract is completed as soon as taken. An Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract is completed when you next acquire The Spice Must Flow.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take one face-up contract and replace it; if all are taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. Completing contracts: Harvest requires a Maker Agent placement and the specified total spice; Immediate completes on taking; Acquire completes when you next acquire the card.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already sending an Agent to that space this turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must have held the contract when you sent the Agent. Once completed, announce it, gain its listed rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: if you take a contract for a space where you ‘already sent your Agent this turn,’ you ‘must wait until a future turn’ and must have held it when sending the Agent. Completion: announce it, gain rewards, flip face down, leave it in supply.

answers.answer: Standard two-player play uses one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival receives the Ornithopter Objective. The two humans are randomly dealt the other two eligible Objectives, and the human whose Objective shows the First Player marker starts. Turn order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between the humans. The Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: use ‘one shared scoring Rival’; give the Rival the Ornithopter Objective; First Player goes to the human whose card shows it; order is ‘First Player → Rival → other human’; Rival ‘never takes a Reveal turn.’

answers.answer: For the occupied destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not send an Agent: place a Spy at an empty post of its specified type, or ignore placement if none exists, then reveal another Hagal card. The Rival ignores normal board-space costs and effects and applies only the Hagal card effects; the summary notes exceptions for Maker and control bonuses. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: ‘Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again.’ Place Spy: use an empty specified post or ignore placement; ‘either way reveal another Hagal card.’ Ignore normal space costs/effects and apply Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
